comment: No source is published. The module hands its work to a Vult-generated delay engine. Two of the three switches wear each other's tooltips: parameter 5 is named RANGE in the maker's own configParam but sits under the panel's MODE heading and selects delay against resonator, and parameter 6 is named MODE but sits under DIRECTION and is passed to the engine as the direction integer. Parameter 4, named RANGE, is the one that really is the OCT RANGE switch: it multiplies the delay time by a half or a third, and adds nought, one or two octaves to the pitch instead. The delay buffer is two seconds of samples capped at 192000. The clock period is only used while a cable is in the clock jack, and the division runs from minus six to plus six through a lookup table. The trigger jack does double duty: it plucks the resonator in one mode and carries the mix CV in the other. The menu item's name is LP filter with a space, colon and space; the module has no other menu of its own.
